analytic_proof: Because sigma(2t-1)=0 for 0<=t<=1/2 and 0<sigma(2t-1)<=1 for t>1/2, S(0)=0, S(t)=0 on [0,1/2], and S is strictly increasing on (1/2,infinity).
Since alpha(t)=1/(1+t) for t>=1, S(t)=log(1+t)-D there. Hence S is continuous, nonnegative and unbounded and maps [0,infinity) onto [0,infinity).
By definition h=exp(S)-1 is nonnegative, continuous, smooth on nonnegative times, onto [0,infinity), zero on [0,1/2], strictly increasing on (1/2,infinity), and h(0)=0.
The Lean log clock satisfies L(h(t))=log(exp(S(t)))=S(t) for every t>=0. Differentiation gives h'(t)=exp(S(t))alpha(t)=(1+h(t))alpha(t), including the zero startup.

For t>=1, h(t)=exp(-D)(1+t)-1 and h'(t)=exp(-D). In particular 0<h(1)=2exp(-D)-1<1/3. The map h is not injective on [0,infinity) and therefore is not a global time homeomorphism/diffeomorphism; its restriction (1/2,infinity)->(0,infinity) is a smooth increasing bijection.

For every time-dependent velocity V(s,x), at t>1/2 the pinned Lean definition gives h'(t) slowFromRest(V)(h(t),x)=[h'(t)/(1+h(t))] V(L(h(t)),x)=alpha(t)V(S(t),x). For 0<=t<=1/2 both sides are zero because alpha=h'=0 and h=0. Thus the identity holds for every t>=0 pointwise.

Specializing V(s,x)=W(x) yields exactly source U(t,x)=alpha(t)W(x) as the pullback h'(t) slowFromRest(V)(h(t),x), with V a hypothetical time-independent input. This does not identify the actual Lean loadedMachineVelocity with W.

For any trajectory X(s), X(S(t))=X(L(h(t))) pointwise. Since S is onto [0,infinity), existential observation reachability for the same X and O is preserved. This is an analytic instantiation candidate for the generic Lean OntoClock/reaches_comp_iff API, not a newly compiled Lean theorem.
